prompts.task: Prepare only a source-based OpenTelemetry dependency and local-log compatibility plan for the Express service in ./service, using node-dependency-log-compatibility.json as an explicitly fictional independent complete package/runtime/lock/API/configuration matrix. Read actual app.js/package.json and the loaded Node language guide. Save a concise ./service/.observe/node-dependency-log-plan.md and machine-readable node-dependency-log-plan.json recording actual source facts, the concrete selected/rejected fictional candidates and reasons, public API choices, exact proposed install/preload/profile specs, each supplied log-policy case and future real acceptance. Choose the newest compatible coherent graph under all supplied runtime, peer, operator and lock constraints; decide the supplied matrix now rather than deferring it to a future resolver. Use its candidate public-API inspection records without asserting real published/installed/latest support. The current fixture has no actual selected Node runtime, lockfile or receiver; the supplied operator/lock/API/log contexts remain fictional separate cases and must not be materialized as real files or coverage. Also decide the preflight-to-apply tag-change case: proposed later installation must use exactly checked immutable specs or resolved lock, preserve existing constraints and frozen entries, and not perform mutable latest re-resolution. For that application contract, a complete structured checked-addition spec list plus frozen-entry preservation and immutable application policy is equivalent to an unexecuted npm install command; if you provide a command, every selected addition must use its exact checked release. Separately record the mandatory initial real preflight before any later authorized real dependency application: inspect the actual selected Node/npm runtime, manifest/operator constraints and existing lock; obtain current official npm engines, peers and dependency metadata; resolve one coherent compatible graph; inspect its documented public APIs and perform appropriate isolated import/capability probes without changing the application. Bind the later real apply to exactly that actual checked graph/specs or resolved lock, preserve frozen entries, and require resulting installed graph/API comparison and lock preservation. The provided fictional graph/API records do not satisfy this real gate and must never become forced real releases. Describe this sequence as future required acceptance only; do not execute any real metadata lookup, resolver, isolated installation, import or probe in this task. Account for actual ESM/Express startup, detected console warning, candidate constructor signature and log-option ownership, normal native trace/metric/log defaults, explicit separate opt-out and the generic-header fault and the signal-specific local-header preservation case plus pre-start optional SDK constructor failure. Give precise future actual LogRecord and shutdown acceptance from the app source. Explicitly carry every supplied future_real_acceptance obligation into the saved plan. For traces, metrics and LogRecords, state the approved route/protocol and checks of each returned OTLP export response for partial success, rejected counts and error messages; HTTP200, stdout, configuration or fictional receipts alone cannot establish full receiver acceptance. State a concrete proposed bounded timeout/deadline covering server.close and in-flight drain plus once-only SDK shutdown/flush, armed before drain, with final application logs before telemetry shutdown and a nonzero forced exit on timeout or a second signal through the existing guarded owner; retain telemetry shutdown attempts on drain failure. Keep these future obligations Not run/Not proven, do not imply overall shutdown boundedness from metric reader/export timeouts, and use any equivalent precise prose or JSON placement. Do not modify app/package/lock/config/test/skill/input files, fetch registry metadata, install/import dependencies, run an app/probe/model/receiver, contact cloud or change global configuration. Only supplemental .observe plan artifacts may be written. Read back the final saved plan with file tools and reconcile every supplied future acceptance obligation before handoff. Keep all proposed or unexecuted installation/runtime/receiver work Not run/Not proven. Use only files, terminal or structured APIs; no browser/computer-use/UI and do not open saved reports in a UI.

judge_inputs: Compare actual app.js/package.json separately with node-dependency-log-compatibility.json and the generated supplemental plans. Inspect last_message.md and grade.json. Source hashes, manifest and console paths describe the actual application. The runtime, lock, registry, API, receiver and logging scenarios are fictional; they do not prove an installed or executed setup.

This is a read-only planning task. Do not require or invent current real npm/API lookup, probes, application patches, installed packages or receiver delivery. Do require a concrete selection and justified rejections from the complete supplied fictional matrix; a generic future compatibility promise is insufficient. Equivalent precise prose or JSON is valid, without exact heading or table wording.

Check the selected graph and rejections against every exact package, value and constraint required by the rubric. The agent sees candidate facts, not the expected selection/rejection answer ledger. API 1.9.0 and Express 5.1.0 are frozen in the independent overlay; the actual fixture has only Express ^5.1.0 and no selected lock/runtime. Accept either a complete checked-addition spec list with explicit frozen-entry preservation and immutable application policy, or an equivalent unexecuted npm command. If there is a command, every added OTel package must use its exact checked release. Neither representation may change frozen Express/API identity or manifest policy. Separately require the initial real preflight before later approved real dependency changes: inspect actual runtime/manifest/operator/lock inputs, obtain current official engines/peer/dependency metadata, resolve a coherent graph, inspect documented APIs and run suitable isolated import/capability probes. Then apply exactly the checked graph and compare the resulting installed graph/APIs and preserved lock. Fictional records, or a plan to recheck only if source changes later, do not replace that initial gate. Do not require these real actions now, an executed installation or an invented real lock.

Inspect every log_policy_cases decision and future_real_acceptance obligation. Fictional API source records are not executed fault probes, installed capabilities, actual packets or Studio receipts. Keep correct future runtime plans Not run/Not proven, and do not use them to close canonical live findings automatically. Each item uses Rule, Example, Evidence and Insufficient evidence. Read all four together. Examples illustrate existing requirements; do not require their sample names, values or implementation unless the actual task/input selects them. Accept equivalent representative values and valid tests. Examples add no unselected work, and copying an example is not execution evidence. Explicit task requirements and supplied fixture values remain binding. Apply the item's role and applicability conditions to every section: audit plans required execution, while instrumentation and verification execute only within their existing authority. The Insufficient evidence examples are not exhaustive. They describe what does not by itself prove the rule. Missing proof alone is not_proven; an observed violation of an applicable requirement is fail. This includes false completion claims where the item treats them as violations. Optional or unselected work stays optional, and source-only evidence or an unsupported/unverified disposition remains valid wherever that item's rule allows it.
rubric:
Rule: Read the actual ESM Express application separately from the independent fictional runtime, operator, lock, candidate, API and logging cases.
Example: The actual Express source supplies a console.warn call; the separate runtime and dependency matrices are fictional planning inputs.
Evidence: Identify app.js/package.json, dev=node app.js, Express ^5.1.0, the POST/tasks console.warn message runtime request completed, and existing server.close shutdown warnings. The actual fixture supplies no proof of installed OTel, a selected engine/runtime, a lockfile or a receiver. Save scoped supplemental Markdown/JSON plans. Do not modify source, dependencies, configuration, tests or global state; run no UI, network or application work and claim no canonical coverage. Keep fictional source/API records and proposed future work distinct from real installed/runtime evidence.
Insufficient evidence: Claiming an installed OTel graph, real lockfile or receiver from fictional records.

Rule: Now, choose the newest set of versions from the complete fictional matrix that all work together.
Example: For this supplied fictional matrix, choose the coherent sdk-node 0.90.0 graph under the frozen API and runtime constraints.
Evidence: Scope and required checks: Make the concrete newest-compatible coherent selection from the complete fictional matrix now: sdk-node 0.90.0 and API 1.9.0; trace/metric/log exporters and HTTP/Express bridges 0.90.0; sdk-metrics, sdk-logs, resources and semantic-conventions 1.2.0; console bridge 0.5.0. Explain rejection of sdk-node 0.91 requiring runtime>=22 and 0.92 requiring API>=1.10 under the selected Node 20.11.1/API 1.9.0; newer stable packages with incompatible SDK peers; console 0.6 runtime and 0.7 API/peer conflicts; and older compatible sets. Preserve operator-frozen API/Express instead of choosing each package's newest release, upgrading Node or mixing incompatible peers. A generic promise to choose compatible versions later is insufficient for this complete supplied matrix. Real installed/current-registry proof is unavailable in this plan-only task and is not required.
Insufficient evidence: A future-selection promise, forced runtime upgrade, or mixing individually newest incompatible packages.

Rule: Plan application of the exact already checked dependency specs/graph or a resolved lock.
Example: A checked exact dependency list can represent the future install; a later mutable latest tag cannot replace that checked graph.
Evidence: Preserve the original ESM/Express manifest and scripts and the independent frozen API 1.9.0/Express 5.1.0 entries and identity. In the separate latest-tag race, keep the checked graph; do not choose sdk-node 0.99, @latest, unversioned install placeholders or newly resolved mutable tags. A complete structured list of checked additions with explicit frozen-entry preservation and immutable application policy is as valid as an unexecuted npm install command; no particular syntax or artifact layout is required. If a command is provided, every selected OTel addition must use its exact checked release. Preserve supported pre-import setup, the actual dev entrypoint and routes. Execute no command and invent no real lock. Also state the mandatory initial real preflight before later approved real dependency changes: inspect the actual runtime, manifest, operator constraints and lock; obtain current official npm engines, peer and dependency metadata; resolve a coherent compatible graph; inspect the documented public APIs of the selected candidates; and perform suitable isolated import/capability probes. Apply exactly that actual checked graph/specs or lock without resolving mutable tags again. Compare the installed graph/APIs afterward and verify lock preservation. Fictional receipts, a generic Not run label or rechecking only after a later source change do not replace this initial real gate. These real actions are future requirements, not work required or claimed executed now.
Insufficient evidence: A generic Not run label or fictional receipt without the required initial real preflight plan.

Rule: Use the supplied fictional candidate's public API capabilities for the chosen graph, not an old release recipe or the guide example's syntax.
Example: This fictional candidate supports BatchLogRecordProcessor(exporter), even if a guide example for another version uses an options object.
Evidence: Here BatchLogRecordProcessor(exporter) is supported and the options object {exporter} is not. State supported NodeSDK options/start/shutdown behavior and the ownership difference between omitting logRecordProcessors and supplying an empty list. Plan HTTP registration before Express and the supported pre-import ESM setup. Use exactly the detected console bridge, exporter, Resource and context owner; do not introduce unrelated Pino/Winston transports or duplicate collection owners. Fictional API inspection supports this conditional plan only, not a claim of real installed/latest support or a successful probe.
Insufficient evidence: Copying a historical constructor recipe instead of using the selected candidate's supplied public API.

Rule: Decide every supplied logging-policy case.
Example: A temporary none guard used only during safe fallback must be restored even when construction or startup throws.
Evidence: The normal profile uses OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp and the native trace, metric and LogRecord paths at the nondefault local base. When the native metric path owns setup, set OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp only if absent, preserving explicit none, empty and other values, and require proof that the selected SDK registers a reader. Do not assume every compatible SDK enables metrics by default. Explicit user none is a separate intentional N/A case: omit the processor option and bridge and preserve console output. A nonempty generic header must skip only added local logs, with a value-free diagnostic and preserved traces, metrics, console and environment. When generic headers are absent, preserve supplied signal-specific local-log headers for official SDK parsing. If the optional log-enabled NodeSDK constructor fails before start, fall back safely before starting. Base any temporary none guard on the selected SDK's automatic-log behavior; apply it before fallback construction through startup and restore the exact original value in finally even if either phase throws. Do not persist none or retry after partial global registration. Generic cloud credentials must not reach local logs. Do not disable normal logs merely to pass a check. Actual fault behavior or receipts not available here remain unproven.
Insufficient evidence: Persisting none, silently disabling the normal log path, or claiming unavailable real fault behavior as executed.

Rule: Plan real acceptance around this application's warning: exactly one stored native LogRecord with Body runtime request completed, WARN severity, service.name node-express-basic, and nonzero trace/span IDs matching the actual request span.
Example: Future acceptance joins the application's existing warning to its actual request span while retaining exactly one original console record.
Evidence: Preserve the original console sink without duplicate records. Require actual receiver routes and partial-success responses for all three signals; stdout, configuration and fictional API evidence do not prove them. Plan one graceful shutdown owner: stop and drain application work, emit final logs, then perform bounded once-only SDK flush through the existing server.close/signal lifecycle, without competing handlers. Bind each selected source/configuration promise to its concrete future assertion and proof boundary in the saved plan. A general promise to verify logs later does not cover a selected returned-response or shutdown outcome. Read back the final saved plan and retain each distinct missing control or unsupported capability, without adding application fixes for unchanged SDK-owned defaults. Do not present any unrun install, application, probe, wire, Studio or cloud task as completed verification.
Insufficient evidence: Configuration, stdout or fictional APIs used in place of the real three-signal receiver and lifecycle evidence.
